SEPARATELY, AND CORRECTING THIS TABLE: the first pass claimed the sixteen items are stored raw. Solving for the weights of the deposit's SDO score returns +1 on all sixteen with a zero intercept, reproducing it for 370 of 370 complete rows, while flipping the eight items the .sav marks (R) reproduces only 32 of 370. They are stored PRE-RECODED. Corroborated by polarity, which points the same way: the across-block correlation is +0.201 rather than negative and the (R) item mean (2.52) sits level with the forward mean (2.45), neither of which a raw table would show. The same test run on sj, rwa and unjust returns PRE-RECODED for all three, so this was a family-wide error. See verify_lys_2020_rape_3_kpnts.R.

Two findings, one of which corrected this table. PAIRING: the Polish comes from Grzesiak-Feldman's cited adaptation (CEEOL id=108624), whose Zalacznik 1 lists twenty numbered items; each of the twelve English labels in the .sav is a direct translation of exactly one of them and vice versa, so the correspondence is forced by content across a 20-item pool rather than assumed from position. It also predicts structure that holds: the six items the appendix marks (R) land exactly on the odd codes rwa1, rwa3, rwa5, rwa7, rwa9, rwa11, an alternating design matching the cons block in the same battery. STORAGE: solving for the weights of the deposit's rwa_sum returns +1 on all twelve with a zero intercept and reproduces it for 342 of 342 complete rows, while flipping the six reverse-worded items reproduces only 22 of 342 -- so the items are stored ALREADY RECODED, correcting this table's original claim that they were raw. That also explains why keying polarity is not usable as a route here: all twelve intercorrelate positively (across-block r = +0.160), exactly as pre-recoding predicts. VERIFIED because the pairing distinguishes every item from every other. NOT established: the response anchors. The appendix publishes a 6-point scale while this study administered 5 (paper and data agree), so its labels do not describe this administration and option_text is blank. DOWNGRADED VERIFIED -> PARTIAL on provenance, not on mapping. The item-to-item correspondence still holds and is if anything stronger than first recorded: besides each English label translating exactly one of twenty appendix items, the lys paper's own three RWA examples -- one per factor -- are appendix items 03, 02 and 04, which independently confirms the appendix contains the study's items. What is NOT verified is that the Polish strings are the administered ones. Radkiewicz's appendix is a 20-item Altemeyer/Duckitt-lineage adaptation (his words: 'wzorowana na tej, ktorej uzywal w swoich badaniach Duckitt'), while the study cites Grzesiak-Feldman's (2012) Polish adaptation of Funke's 12-item scale -- a different adaptation, which Radkiewicz never cites. So item_text is canonical_instrument rather than study_materials, and the English twin from the study's own .sav is the better record of the administration.

The source states the mapping and the response data confirms it. STATED: the deposit's Codebook sheet keys Q1..Q12 to their statements, and data/kfcovid_Li2020/'knowledge and fear of covid_ knowledge scale.do' reshapes `Q1 Q2 ... Q12 -> Q` renaming the reshape index to `item`, so the live bare integer is the Q number rather than an opaque index. The Codebook and Survey 1 sheets are byte-identical on 11 of 12 statements, an internal cross-check; the 12th is readable only in Survey 1 because the Codebook's Q4 cell is a broken reference ('0x17'). CONFIRMED: the workbook's Survey 1 sheet publishes % Correct per item, and the observed proportion of resp == 1 reproduces all twelve values exactly, max absolute difference 0.000e+00. That also proves resp encodes CORRECTNESS rather than the answer -- item 9, a False statement, shows 0.9909, where a literal-answer coding would show 0.0091. LIMIT of the %-correct route taken alone: four items share 0.990909 and two share 0.972727, so the percentages by themselves leave those groups interchangeable (48 of 479,001,600 orderings fit). VERIFIED rests on the stated mapping, which names every item; the percentages corroborate it and would have caught a wrong ordering outside those ties. Item sets match at 12 items and resp sets match at 0/1 -- both axes pass, which an intermediate raw_resp version did not achieve: it left resp empty, so the gate skipped the resp check instead of passing it, and SKILL.md reserves raw_resp for cases where no scoring key exists at all. option_text and correct_response are blank as behavior-scored; the answer key is recorded in provenance.

The codebook states the mapping item by item and the response ranges corroborate it. STATED: Codebook_Baseline.xlsx rows 124-137 give one row per item carrying its own wording and its own response ladder, keyed by a cleandata_pre column reading Q102..Q115; data/mhscdc_fried_2020.r selects num_range("Pre", 102:115) and pivots with names_to = "item", a number-preserving rename with no positional step. CORROBORATED: each item's observed range sits inside its own declared ladder, and the ladder lengths differ across section 2 in a way that would expose a misalignment -- Pre114 tops out at exactly 4 against a 4-level ladder, while Pre112 and Pre115 reach 5 and 7 against 6- and 8-level ladders because two offered levels went unchosen. Had the four general-use items been permuted, an item would have shown a response above its ladder length; none does. LIMIT: within section 1 the ten SAS items all share one 6-point ladder, so range alone does not separate them from each other -- their individual assignment rests on the codebook naming each one, which it does. Item sets match at 14 items, resp sets match.

The deposit's variable dictionary names all 36 mathwrit_std35_* variables and the live code is that name with the wave prefix stripped; the dictionary's 36 codes and the live 36 are the same set exactly. Because the renaming happened upstream of this repo (data/gilbert_hte/postprocessing.R points at an external analysis directory), the correspondence was tested against the data rather than read off a script, using a prediction the dictionary makes and the responses can refute: a code the dictionary defines only with a b_ prefix must appear only at wave 0, and one defined only with e1_/e2_ must never appear at wave 0. Six codes are baseline-only (hvy_obj, sol_a..sol_e) and five endline-only (add3d_c, add3d_d, mul_d, mul_e, subt3d_d), so 11 of 36 are testable, and all 11 hold -- the six appear at wave 0 alone, the five at waves 0.5 and 1 only, and all 25 remaining codes span baseline and endline as predicted. PARTIAL for two reasons. First, the route does not separate the 25 all-wave codes from each other, nor members of a task family from each other; their assignment rests on the dictionary naming each variable. Second and more important, the shipped item_text is a task description rather than the literal problem, because the study used four parallel forms with differing numerals and the live table records no form -- so several items share identical item_text by necessity. Item sets match at 36, resp sets at 0/1.
